name: Ezri
overview: Ezri was a male from the tribe of Judah who held a significant administrative role during King David's reign. He was responsible for overseeing David's agricultural workers, indicating a position of trust and management in the royal household. His lineage is noted as the son of Chelub, which situates him within a known family line in Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezri means 'my help,' reflecting a personal name of Hebrew origin. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful designation that may imply a supportive or assisting role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ezri as the son of Chelub. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded, so his familial connections are limited to this paternal link as stated in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ezri's significance lies in his administrative responsibility over agricultural workers during the reign of David, highlighting the organized governance and stewardship within the kingdom. His role demonstrates the practical aspects of David's administration and the reliance on capable leaders from the tribe of Judah. This position also reflects the broader biblical theme of faithful service and order under God's appointed king.
